newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada cutting unemployment premium from 1998.
newsitem.headline: Canada cutting unemployment premium from 1998.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Friday that as part of a deal with Ontario, the federal government would cut the unemployment insurance premium slightly from the start of 1998.
He said the rate would decline to C$2.80 per C$100 of insurable earnings from the current C$2.90.

Ottawa had already budgeted for a five-cent decline, and Martin said it was possible that another five cents could have been announced in November. Ontario asked for this to be announced now, a request he acceded to during negotiations over increases in premiums for the Canada Pension Plan.
Toronto's Globe and Mail newspaper said every five-cent cut costs the government C$325 million in revenue.
